system.description:
Origins

Tieflings are the Aasimar's counterpart on the side of Chaos, created to be its servants. They vary far more in appearance, usually bearing several mutations that mark them as its servants — hooves, tails, claws and horns are all common. Many obey their gods' every whim, but a large share simply do as they please, which serves Chaos just as well. Like the Aasimar they are recruited from other races, but instead of orderly training the process involves agonising bodily transformation and promises of power.

True Tiefling society barely exists. Most live barbarically for their own desires and indulge every impulse, which makes them extremely unpredictable — a gang might loot some houses, burn others, paint gorgeous murals on the rest and turn someone's lawn into a lovely garden.

Appearance

Born from roiling chaos, Tieflings differ enormously in looks and physiology. Each was once a member of another race, remade through ceremony and ritual (and occasionally by accident). Most serve the Ruinous Powers and were changed to serve them better; fighting comes naturally to them, and although a little smaller than Aasimar on average, just as tough.

They are generally humanoid but always show some touch of chaos, such as cloven hooves, lizard-like tails, horns or an unearthly beauty. Their former race says little about their new form, although their general appearance can hint at the power that changed them. Where every Aasimar is the same masterpiece, each Tiefling is unique — stronger or weaker, lovelier or more hideous, but always one of a kind.

In Play

Tieflings revel in their power. They serve the Ruinous Powers out of their own desires rather than pure duty or faith. Where the Aasimar lose themselves in rebirth, a Tiefling's true self is made flesh: their new form is shaped partly by their soul and hidden wishes and reflects who they are deep down. What they remember of their previous life is blurry, yet the essentials survive: the motives that led them to this transformation.

Every Tiefling is, at heart, someone who valued personal ambition above loyalty to their people. They are less committed to the Blood War than the Aasimar but far more numerous, since the Ruinous Powers can create one and turn it loose far more easily than the Blessed Pantheon can raise its servants. Not all of them serve Chaos: just as some Aasimar turn to the Ruinous Powers, some Tieflings choose a more dependable master.

Relations

Tieflings are overwhelmingly distrusted and often treated as mutants or monsters. Their old family ties are cut, and many factions and whole worlds refuse to deal with them. Most see this as a small price for their power — they were often shunned for their deeds already.

Example heroes (p. 51): Traya, Petticoat, Shax.
